title: Should Air Vents Be Open or Closed?

content_html:
In most ducted heating and cooling systems, supply registers should remain open unless the system was specifically designed and balanced otherwise. Closing several increases duct pressure and can reduce airflow through the equipment instead of usefully sending all that air to other rooms.

Keep normal supply registers open

An adjustable register can support small comfort changes, but fully closing it changes system resistance. Start with registers open and correct balancing causes before using extreme closure.

Do not block return-air grilles

Return grilles let the system pull air back from the home. Furniture, rugs, or improvised filters in front of them reduce airflow and can increase noise and blower load.

An uncomfortable room needs diagnosis, not just closing other vents

Uneven temperature can come from duct leakage, insulation, solar exposure, or inadequate airflow. Closing registers in comfortable rooms may hide the cause while creating new issues.

Zoned systems are a designed exception

Motorized dampers and zone controls are designed to vary airflow in a coordinated way. A manually closed register is not equivalent to a zoned system; follow the equipment’s specific design and maintenance guidance.

faq.answer: An adjustable register can support small comfort changes, but fully closing it changes system resistance. Start with registers open and correct balancing causes before using extreme closure.

faq.question: Why should return-air grilles stay unblocked?
faq.answer: Return grilles let the system pull air back from the home. Furniture, rugs, or improvised filters in front of them reduce airflow and can increase noise and blower load.

faq.question: Is a zoned system the same as manually closing vents?
faq.answer: Motorized dampers and zone controls are designed to vary airflow in a coordinated way. A manually closed register is not equivalent to a zoned system; follow the equipment’s specific design and maintenance guidance.
